Adults enter the Fraser River from April to August (Bradford and Taylor 2023, p. 131, citing COSEWIC 2018), across the region's spring and summer runs, so the start is the region's, not Swift Creek's. The window ends the day before NuSEDS's median start of spawning (08-11), as BULK's migration ends where its spawning starts; NuSEDS's median stream arrival is 08-01 (125 population-years, 1967-2000). NuSEDS's start of spawning is an estimate, not the first spawner seen: read as the bulk of spawning it is 08-12, and 11 records whose survey of three or more visits began before the start put it at 08-15 (research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).

NuSEDS release 20260601: median START_SPAWN_DT_FROM to median END_SPAWN_DT_TO (else END_SPAWN_DT_FROM) over 123 and 126 population-years, 1967-2000, of the populations on streams wholly in UFRA by FWA watershed code, plus the Fraser mainstem above Tete Jaune (data-raw/timing_nuseds.R, scripts/logs/timing/20261118_timing_nuseds.txt). Swift Creek alone 08-09 to 09-05 (27 years); the mainstem above Tete Jaune ends later (median 09-20, 15 years). No spawn dates after 2000. Candy et al. 2002 (Appendix 1) give 2001 peak spawning weeks of 8/16-8/23 at Swift Creek to 8/31-9/7 on the Fraser at Tete Jaune. NuSEDS's start and end dates are estimates, not the first and last spawners seen (82 of these 123 starts fall on DFO's five-day grid, and 28 of the 75 with a survey's first day precede it), so they support the middle of this window and cannot test its edges. Read as the bulk of spawning (bins as midpoints, records whose adults were present) it runs 08-12 to 09-05 over 124 and 126 population-years, peaking about 08-24 (172 peaks, 1967-2014: after 2000 DFO gives only peaks); its start of 08-15 rests on 11 records whose survey of three or more visits began before it (scripts/logs/timing/20261124_timing_nuseds.txt, research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).

The Cottonwood population passes the lower Fraser very early, April-May (Candy et al. 2002, p. 22). The window ends the day before NuSEDS's median start of spawning (08-10), as BULK's migration ends where its spawning starts; NuSEDS's median stream arrival is 08-01 (23 population-years). NuSEDS's start of spawning is an estimate, not the first spawner seen: read as the bulk of spawning it is the same day, 08-10, and no record has the survey to stand for an edge (research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).

NuSEDS release 20260601: median START_SPAWN_DT_FROM to median END_SPAWN_DT_TO (else END_SPAWN_DT_FROM) over 35 and 36 population-years, 1953-2009, of three populations on streams wholly in COTR by FWA watershed code (data-raw/timing_nuseds.R, scripts/logs/timing/20261118_timing_nuseds.txt): the Swift River (a Cottonwood tributary) 08-05 to 09-01 (21 years, 1953-1974), Naver Creek 08-13 to 09-10 (10 years) and a second Swift River population 07-28 to 09-20 (4 years). The Cottonwood River's own records carry no spawn dates, and most dated years are before 1975. Candy et al. 2002 (Appendix 1) give 2001 peak spawning weeks of 8/21-8/28 for the Cottonwood and 8/19-8/26 for Naver Creek. NuSEDS's start and end dates are estimates, not the first and last spawners seen (19 of these 35 starts fall on DFO's five-day grid, and 12 of the 32 with a survey's first day precede it), so they support the middle of this window and cannot test its edges. Read as the bulk of spawning (bins as midpoints, records whose adults were present) it runs 08-10 to 09-05 over 35 and 36 population-years, peaking about 08-24 (40 peaks, 1953-2008); no record has the survey to stand for an edge (scripts/logs/timing/20261124_timing_nuseds.txt, research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).
